claims.text: Temperature and humidity have a cause-and-effect relationship with the onset or suppression of corrosion-related degradation in Q235 steel.
Variation of temperature and humidity can promote formation of a protective oxide layer on Q235 steel.
Variation of temperature and humidity can cause breakdown of the passive film on Q235 steel.
Temperature and humidity influence the kinetics of corrosion reactions in Q235 steel.
Changes in corrosion-reaction kinetics lead to formation or degradation of the protective oxide layer.
At 80°C and 80% relative humidity, Q235 steel will exhibit a 30% higher corrosion rate than the reference at 20°C and 40% relative humidity.
The proposed applicability range is 20°C to 80°C and 40% to 80% relative humidity.
The presence of corrosive species may alter the relationship between temperature, humidity, and corrosion rate.
Surface roughness may alter the relationship between temperature, humidity, and corrosion rate.
